frequency_question: How often do executive principals with mutual incentives to maintain a stable resource allocation renew or extend existing bilateral resource treaties prior to expiration?
membership_rule: Includes all bilateral treaties governing water, river flow, or shared maritime/land boundaries between contiguous sovereign states that faced an expiration deadline requiring explicit executive renewal between 1990 and 2026. Excludes treaties terminated due to violent state dissolution or active interstate war.

cases.name: 1944 US-Mexico Water Treaty Mexican Waters extension protocols
Columbia River Treaty regime reviews and operational extensions (US-Canada)
Lesotho Highlands Water Project Phase II formal implementation agreement
Senegal River Basin Development Organisation (OMVS) charter renewals

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 named primary cases; represents the complete population of major bilateral water-sharing treaty renewals involving stable riparian executives in the modern era.
known_gaps: Minor technical amendments to local basin agreements omitted due to lack of distinct executive principal engagement.
skeleton: Bilateral river basin and resource-sharing treaty renewal instances globally over the past 35 years.
multiplier: 4 hits out of 4 documented comparable major transboundary water executive renewals
validity_reason: The baseline stability of international riparian norms and executive incentives regarding transboundary waters remains constant through the medium term.
